title: Widget lineage & Signal Garden playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic approach to widget (panel) lineage, how UI panels map to underlying probes/metrics/traces, and a lightweight playbook for onboarding, triage handoffs, and dashboard cost pruning. It tries to be implementation-friendly: concrete tag names, a minimal trace handoff contract, and a checklist for feature rollouts.

Background & motivation:
- We have increasing dashboard sprawl. Operators can't easily see which spans/queries back a panel. During incidents this costs time and increases blast radius.
- Some panels are expensive (high cardinality SQL or heavy trace joins) and lack owner or test coverage.
- Model and rollout churn (new model versions, quantized variants) changes metric definitions; we need a lineage-first view so dashboards remain trustable.

Goals:
- Every production-facing panel has a documented lineage: probe(s), span/tag anchors, query id, and owner.
- A minimal trace handoff convention so traces link back to user/customer/session contexts for repro.
- A lightweight pruning rubric for panels with poor ROI.
- Onboarding checklist new features must satisfy before dashboard rollout.

Signal Garden Concepts (terms we use):
- Probe: the instrumentation point that emits a specific metric or event (e.g., kvcache.hits, request.latency.v2).
- Anchor tag: a short set of trace/span tags used to correlate dashboard rows with trace data (e.g., tenant_id, model_name, route).
- Widget lineage: mapping of panel -> probe(s) -> query id -> owner -> SLIs.
- Signal Garden: the living index (not yet a product; currently a doc + tag conventions) of probes and their owners.

Minimal panel lineage template (must be in panel notes):
- Panel name: short descriptive title (avoid "Latency" alone).
- Primary probe(s): comma-separated metric names (prometheus/ingest event name).
- Trace anchor tags: list (tenant_id, request_id, model_variant).
- Query id / raw source: dataset/table + query id or metric ingestion job name.
- Owner: person/team.
- SLI mapping: SLI name + alert threshold + aggregation (p95 p99).
- Cost estimate: query 1-run cost / cardinality notes.
- Last validated: YYYY-MM-DD + validation note/PR.

Example (text representation for a panel):
Panel name: "Generate API p95 by model variant"
Primary probes: api.request.latency_ms, api.tokens_generated.count
Trace anchor tags: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant
Query id: metrics.sql:dashboard_gen_p95_v2 (run joins with token table)
Owner: eng-serving-runtime / runbook lead: Priya Nair
SLI mapping: p95(api.request.latency_ms) > 800ms -> P4 alert; p99 > 1200ms -> P2
Cost estimate: high (joins on tokens table, cardinality by tenant ~10k/day)
Last validated: 2026-01-28 (PR #512)

Probe->Panel mapping heuristics:
- 1 probe -> many panels is ok (aggregate slices), but every panel must list the primary probe.
- Panels that compute heavy percentiles across high-cardinality dimensions should have a cached rollup probe. If none exists, flag for engineering.
- If a panel uses derived metrics (ratio of two probes), list both probes and the derivation to avoid silent drift.

Trace handoff contract (minimal):
- When an operator clicks "open trace" from a panel, the frontend should supply: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, panel_query_id.
- Trace collectors must ensure these tags are present on the root span. Use tag names: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, route. Keep tag values short (no long payloads).
- Sampling: adaptive sampling recommended. For errors and high-latency (> p95) always sample full traces. For baseline traffic sample at 0.1% with deterministic reservoir by tenant_id to preserve tenant coverage.

Tagging conventions (short list we should enforce):
- tenant_id (string)
- request_id (uuid)
- model_name (string)
- model_variant (string: e.g., llama-70b-q4f)
- route (string: /v1/generate)
- probe_version (string): small tag to indicate metric definition version

Dashboard pruning rubric (quick decision tree):
- Age < 90 days and owner assigned -> keep.
- Owner unassigned and last_validation > 180 days -> mark for review.
- Query cost > threshold (TBD) and usage by stakeholders < 3/month -> archive.
- Panels that duplicate other existing panels (>= 80% overlapping probes + same filters) -> consolidate.

Onboarding checklist for new feature / model rollout (must be signed off before panel creation):
- [ ] Instrumentation: probes added with owner and probe_version tag.
- [ ] Trace anchors included in root span for end-to-end repro.
- [ ] Dashboard panel lineage doc created and linked (path + query id).
- [ ] Cost estimate for panel queries and rollups documented.
- [ ] SLIs defined, threshold proposed, escalation owner noted.
- [ ] A canary dashboard with synthetic probe(s) created for rollout window.

Quick instrumentation notes for engineers (practical):
- Emit single probes for simple counters; avoid post-ingest aggregation in metric name. Keep derivative math in dashboards with explicit formulas.
- For latency probes, emit buckets (histogram) + summary pre-aggregates where feasible. Use tags sparingly and rely on pre-aggregated labels for high-cardinality dims.
- Add a probe_version tag when changing metric semantics (counts vs samples). That makes rollback detection easier.

Operational play: incident triage flow using widget lineage:
1) Pager hits for SLO -> operator opens impacted dashboard panel.
2) Panel lineage section shows primary probe and query id; operator clicks "open trace" -> request_id forwarded to trace UI.
3) If trace shows model_variant mismatch or high kv-eviction, operator escalates to eng-serving-runtime.
4) Owner runs lineage checklist (validate probe version, confirm last validation). If missing, owner opens OBS-324 and tags relevant people.

Open questions / trade-offs (notes to discuss in next workshop):
- Where do we store the Signal Garden index? Confluence piles up; should we migrate to a lightweight DB or use labels inside the metric registry?
- Cost threshold numbers: need a simple weekly query-cost dashboard to derive sane thresholds.
- How to enforce tag hygiene across languages (python, go, rust)? Suggest a small shared lib for tag constants.

Immediate next actions (short):
- (Evan) Draft a templated PANEL_NOTES.md file and add to dashboard repo (due 2026-02-10).
- (Priya) Run a query-cost sweep on top-200 dashboard queries (OBS-324) and return a candidate cutoff by 2026-02-17.
- (Samir) Prototype trace handoff link in trace UI for at least two panels by 2026-02-24.
- Run 1-hour workshop (owners + SRE + console UX) to agree on panel lineage template and enforcement (proposed 2026-02-12).

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- Could encode lineage as small YAML frontmatter attached to panels in the UI, then export to a Signal Garden index.
- Consider a microservice that responds to panel_query_id -> list(probes, owners, last_validated). That would speed up operator flows.
- Remember: small explicit tags beat massive freeform request metadata. Keep it tidy.

References & links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/obs-widget-lineage
- PR for metric change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/512
- Jira: OBS-324 (query cost sweep)
- Slack discussion: #ops-observability thread-T12345

Appendix: quick ASCII matrix (probe categories)
- ingestion: request.count, request.bytes, request.latency_ms
- storage: kvcache.hits, kvcache.miss, kvcache.evictions
- compute: model.token.count, model.attention.sparsity, model.infer.gpu_ms
- quality: rerank.precision, hallucination.rate (operator-reviewed samples)

End of doc.
